record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Function Field Arithmetic — The Influence of John Tate’s Work
record.original_question: As E ranges over elliptic curves defined over Q, are the arithmetic ranks and analytic ranks of E(Q) bounded, or can they become arbitrarily large?

evidence.quote: It is not known whether the (arithmetic or analytic) ranks of E(Q) are bounded as E runs through elliptic curves E over Q, the usual bet seems to be that they are not.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider elliptic curves $E$ defined over the field of rational numbers $\mathbb{Q}$. By the Mordell–Weil theorem, the abelian group $E(\mathbb{Q})$ of rational points is finitely generated, and hence isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}^r \oplus T$ for some non-negative integer $r$ (the arithmetic rank) and finite torsion subgroup $T$. The analytic rank of $E$ is defined to be the order of vanishing at $s = 1$ of the Hasse–Weil $L$-function $L(E,s)$.

Question: As $E$ varies over all elliptic curves defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, is there an absolute constant $C$ such that the arithmetic rank of $E(\mathbb{Q})$ is at most $C$? Equivalently, does $\sup_E \mathrm{rank}\, E(\mathbb{Q}) < \infty$? The analogous question is asked for the analytic rank of $E$.
artifact.status_search_result: The boundedness of ranks of elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ is a well-known open problem. Recent heuristics (Park, Poonen, Voight, Wood, 2019) suggest ranks should be bounded, with only finitely many curves of rank greater than 21, but this is not proved. Explicit examples are known with rank at least 29 (Elkies–Klagsbrun, 2024). The analytic rank version is similarly unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Rank of an elliptic curve - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is in general an open problem whether the rank of all elliptic curves over a fixed field K is bounded by a number or not.

status_evidence.title: A heuristic for boundedness of ranks of elliptic curves
status_evidence.snippet: A heuristic suggests that ranks of elliptic curves E over Q are bounded, and in fact, suggests that there are only finitely many E of rank greater than 21.
status_evidence.claim: Heuristics predict boundedness but no proof is known.
